answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a stake that is slashed when the same behaviour pattern appears across several accounts — like a falcon spotting one hunter wearing many disguises. New identities start with near-zero trust and must earn standing slowly through verified, useful work, so an operator spinning up thousands of clones pays a real cost per clone while harvesting only nectar-thin rewards until each proves itself. Long-lived identities build a relic-like record that cannot be bought instantly, making fake armies expensive and slow to build.
